properties.name: A gap acknowledgement must expire when the thing it judged changes, not only when the SET of affected nodes changes
properties.statement:
`acknowledge_gap`'s own tool description promises: "If the gap's affected nodes later change, the review expires and the gap returns for a fresh judgement." That promise is only half kept. A gap id hashes its `gap_source` and its affected node IDS, so the review expires when the affected SET changes membership — and never when the affected NODES change content.

FOUND BY TRIPPING OVER IT, 2026-07-30, minutes after the requirements involved were accepted. `req:graph-indexes-snapshots` and `req:plans-move-honestly` were both parked on 2026-07-28 with their `unsatisfied_requirement` gaps acknowledged, each reason reading "Deferred on Anthony's word … scheduled for a later increment rather than built now." Anthony then accepted both as intent on 2026-07-30 and neither raised a gap, because a review written about a DEFERRED requirement silently went on suppressing the gap for an ACCEPTED one. Two requirements he had just committed to were invisible as open work.

THE SHARPER INSTANCE IS THE SAME NODE. `req:graph-indexes-snapshots` was reworded in the same session, off git-ref indexing and onto answering temporal questions in the graph. Its acknowledgement's rationale still reads "the graph owns the MAP from epoch/increment to the git ref that holds it" — so an accepted review was left justifying a requirement that no longer says that, and nothing noticed. A review that outlives the wording it reviewed is worse than no review, because it reads as a human having agreed to something they never saw.

WHAT CHANGES SHOULD EXPIRE A REVIEW, and this is the part to decide rather than assume: a status move (proposed → accepted is the case that bit), a statement rewrite, or any property the review's reasoning depended on. The honest difficulty is that reflow2 cannot know which properties a free-text rationale depended on, so the candidate rules are (a) expire on any property change to an affected node, which is safe and noisy; (b) expire on status change plus statement change only, which is targeted and guesses; (c) record what the review was made AGAINST — a content hash of the affected nodes at review time — and expire when that hash moves, which is the same mechanism `set_artifact_checksum` already uses for as-built drift and needs no guessing about which properties mattered.

(c) LOOKS RIGHT AND IS ALREADY A PATTERN HERE: an artifact's registered checksum is exactly "what I accepted, as it was when I accepted it", and a mismatch is reported rather than assumed harmless. A review is the same shape one level up.

NOT THE SAME DEFECT AS `req:set-scoped-acknowledgement-keys-on-its-rule`, and worth stating because they are mirror images and a fix for one could easily break the other. That requirement was about acknowledgements expiring TOO EAGERLY — a project-level rollup whose member set grows on every capability, so a standing judgement could never carry. This is the opposite failure: a per-node review that does not expire when it should. One is a false alarm, the other a false silence, and the pair suggests the underlying model — expiry keyed on an id hash — is too blunt for both.

Captured 2026-07-30 while promoting the planning axis to intent. The two stale acknowledgements found were withdrawn immediately so the accepted requirements show as open work; this requirement is about the mechanism, not those two instances.
